passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Chisel out two stone tablets like the originals, and I will write on them the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to chisel two stone tablets.
The LORD said the tablets must be like the first ones.
The LORD said, "I will write on these tablets."
The LORD said, "I will write the same words that were on the first tablets."
Moses had broken the first tablets.
The LORD will replace the words that were lost.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה פְּסָל־ לְךָ֛ שְׁנֵֽי־ לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִ֖ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֑ים וְכָתַבְתִּי֙ עַל־ הַלֻּחֹ֔ת אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֛וּ עַל־ הַלֻּחֹ֥ת הָרִאשֹׁנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שִׁבַּֽרְתָּ׃

passages.text: Be ready in the morning, and come up on Mount Sinai to present yourself before Me on the mountaintop.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses instructions.
The LORD told Moses to prepare himself.
The LORD said, “Be ready in the morning.”
The LORD commanded Moses to come up Mount Sinai in the morning.
The LORD told Moses to stand before Him on the top of the mountain.
passages.original: וֶהְיֵ֥ה נָכ֖וֹן לַבֹּ֑קֶר וְעָלִ֤יתָ בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ אֶל־ הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וְנִצַּבְתָּ֥ לִ֛י שָׁ֖ם עַל־ רֹ֥אשׁ הָהָֽר׃

passages.text: No one may go up with you; in fact, no one may be seen anywhere on the mountain—not even the flocks or herds may graze in front of the mountain.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave Moses a command.
No person may go up the mountain with you.
No person may be seen anywhere on the mountain.
No flocks may graze in front of the mountain.
No herds may graze in front of the mountain.
passages.original: וְאִישׁ֙ לֹֽא־ יַעֲלֶ֣ה עִמָּ֔ךְ וְגַם־ אִ֥ישׁ אַל־ יֵרָ֖א בְּכָל־ הָהָ֑ר גַּם־ הַצֹּ֤אן וְהַבָּקָר֙ אַל־ יִרְע֔וּ אֶל־ מ֖וּל הָהָ֥ר הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: So Moses chiseled out two stone tablets like the originals. He rose early in the morning, and taking the two stone tablets in his hands, he went up Mount Sinai as the LORD had commanded him.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
God had commanded Moses to come up Mount Sinai.
Moses chiseled out two stone tablets.
These tablets were like the first ones.
Moses got up early in the morning.
He took the two stone tablets in his hands.
Moses went up Mount Sinai.
He did exactly as the LORD had commanded him.
passages.original: וַיִּפְסֹ֡ל שְׁנֵֽי־ לֻחֹ֨ת אֲבָנִ֜ים כָּרִאשֹׁנִ֗ים וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם מֹשֶׁ֤ה בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וַיַּ֙עַל֙ אֶל־ הַ֣ר סִינַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֹת֑וֹ וַיִּקַּ֣ח בְּיָד֔וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י לֻחֹ֥ת אֲבָנִֽים׃

passages.text: And the LORD descended in a cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed His name, the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD came down in a cloud.
The LORD stood there with Moses.
The LORD announced His own name.
The LORD said, “The LORD.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֤רֶד יְהוָה֙ בֶּֽעָנָ֔ן וַיִּתְיַצֵּ֥ב עִמּ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם וַיִּקְרָ֥א בְשֵׁ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Then the LORD passed in front of Moses and called out: “The LORD, the LORD God, is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion and faithfulness, maintaining loving devotion to a thousand generations, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers on their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generations.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD is compassionate.
The LORD is gracious.
The LORD is slow to anger.
The LORD abounds in loving devotion.
The LORD abounds in faithfulness.
The LORD maintains loving devotion to a thousand generations.
The LORD forgives iniquity.
The LORD forgives transgression.
The LORD forgives sin.
The LORD does not leave the guilty unpunished.
The LORD visits the iniquity of the fathers on their children.
The LORD visits the iniquity of the fathers on their grandchildren.
The LORD visits the iniquity of the fathers to the third generation.
The LORD visits the iniquity of the fathers to the fourth generation.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה׀ עַל־ פָּנָיו֮ וַיִּקְרָא֒ יְהוָ֣ה׀ יְהוָ֔ה אֵ֥ל רַח֖וּם וְחַנּ֑וּן אֶ֥רֶךְ אַפַּ֖יִם וְרַב־ חֶ֥סֶד וֶאֱמֶֽת׀ נֹצֵ֥ר חֶ֙סֶד֙ לָאֲלָפִ֔ים נֹשֵׂ֥א עָוֺ֛ן וָפֶ֖שַׁע וְחַטָּאָ֑ה וְנַקֵּה֙ לֹ֣א יְנַקֶּ֔ה פֹּקֵ֣ד׀ עֲוֺ֣ן אָב֗וֹת עַל־ בָּנִים֙ וְעַל־ בְּנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים עַל־ שִׁלֵּשִׁ֖ים וְעַל־ רִבֵּעִֽים׃

passages.text: Moses immediately bowed down to the ground and worshiped.
passages.sermon:
Moses was present with the LORD.
Moses acted quickly.
Moses bowed down to the ground.
Moses worshiped the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְמַהֵ֖ר מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּקֹּ֥ד אַ֖רְצָה וַיִּשְׁתָּֽחוּ׃

passages.text: “O Lord,” he said, “if I have indeed found favor in Your sight, my Lord, please go with us. Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin, and take us as Your inheritance.”
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the Lord.
Moses had just bowed down and worshiped God.
Moses said, “O Lord, if I have found favor in Your sight, please go with us.”
The people of Israel are stubborn and rebellious.
Forgive our iniquity and our sin.
Take us as Your inheritance.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֡אמֶר אִם־ נָא֩ מָצָ֨אתִי חֵ֤ן בְּעֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ אֲדֹנָ֔י יֵֽלֶךְ־ נָ֥א אֲדֹנָ֖י בְּקִרְבֵּ֑נוּ כִּ֤י עַם־ קְשֵׁה־ עֹ֙רֶף֙ ה֔וּא וְסָלַחְתָּ֛ לַעֲוֺנֵ֥נוּ וּלְחַטָּאתֵ֖נוּ וּנְחַלְתָּֽנוּ׃

passages.text: And the LORD said, “Behold, I am making a covenant. Before all your people I will perform wonders that have never been done in any nation in all the world. All the people among whom you live will see the LORD’s work, for it is an awesome thing that I am doing with you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “I am making a covenant with you.”
The LORD said, “I will do wonders before all your people.”
These wonders have never happened in any nation in all the world.
All the people among whom you live will see the work of the LORD.
The LORD’s work is awesome.
I am doing this awesome thing with you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֣ה אָנֹכִי֮ כֹּרֵ֣ת בְּרִית֒ נֶ֤גֶד כָּֽל־ עַמְּךָ֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה נִפְלָאֹ֔ת אֲשֶׁ֛ר לֹֽא־ נִבְרְא֥וּ בְכָל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבְכָל־ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְרָאָ֣ה כָל־ הָ֠עָם אֲשֶׁר־ אַתָּ֨ה בְקִרְבּ֜וֹ אֶת־ מַעֲשֵׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי־ נוֹרָ֣א ה֔וּא אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י עֹשֶׂ֥ה עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Observe what I command you this day. I will drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God gave them commands on that day.
God told them to obey His commands.
God said, “Observe what I command you today.”
God promised to act for them.
God said, “I will drive out your enemies before you.”
God named these enemies.
They are the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
God Himself will remove these nations from before Israel.
passages.original: שְׁמָ֨ר־ לְךָ֔ אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י מְצַוְּךָ֣ הַיּ֑וֹם הִנְנִ֧י גֹרֵ֣שׁ מִפָּנֶ֗יךָ אֶת־ הָאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וְהַחִתִּי֙ וְהַפְּרִזִּ֔י וְהַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִֽי׃

passages.text: Be careful not to make a treaty with the inhabitants of the land you are entering, lest they become a snare in your midst.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God warned them about the land they would enter.
God said, "Be careful."
Do not make a treaty with the people who live in that land.
If you make a treaty with them, they will become a trap for you.
They will cause trouble among you.
passages.original: הִשָּׁ֣מֶר לְךָ֗ פֶּן־ תִּכְרֹ֤ת בְּרִית֙ לְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה בָּ֣א עָלֶ֑יהָ פֶּן־ יִהְיֶ֥ה לְמוֹקֵ֖שׁ בְּקִרְבֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: Rather, you must tear down their altars, smash their sacred stones, and chop down their Asherah poles.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God commanded them to destroy the religious objects of the people living in the land.
You must tear down their altars.
You must smash their sacred stones.
You must cut down their Asherah poles.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֶת־ מִזְבְּחֹתָם֙ תִּתֹּצ֔וּן וְאֶת־ מַצֵּבֹתָ֖ם תְּשַׁבֵּר֑וּן וְאֶת־ אֲשֵׁרָ֖יו תִּכְרֹתֽוּן׃

passages.text: For you must not worship any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD’s name is Jealous.
The LORD is a jealous God.
Do not worship any other god.
passages.original: כִּ֛י לֹ֥א תִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֖ה לְאֵ֣ל אַחֵ֑ר כִּ֤י יְהוָה֙ קַנָּ֣א שְׁמ֔וֹ אֵ֥ל קַנָּ֖א הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, for when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to them, they will invite you, and you will eat their sacrifices.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God warned them about the people living in the land of Canaan.
Do not make a covenant with the people who live in the land.
These people worship other gods.
They turn away from the true God.
They offer sacrifices to their false gods.
They may invite you to join them.
If you accept their invitation, you will eat food from their sacrifices.
This will lead you away from God.
passages.original: פֶּן־ תִּכְרֹ֥ת בְּרִ֖ית לְיוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְזָנ֣וּ׀ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֗ם וְזָבְחוּ֙ לֵאלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם וְקָרָ֣א לְךָ֔ וְאָכַלְתָּ֖ מִזִּבְחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And when you take some of their daughters as brides for your sons, their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and cause your sons to do the same.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God warned them about the people living in the land.
If you take their daughters as wives for your sons, trouble will come.
Their daughters will worship their own gods.
Their daughters will lead your sons to worship those same gods.
Your sons will turn away from God because of this.
passages.original: וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ מִבְּנֹתָ֖יו לְבָנֶ֑יךָ וְזָנ֣וּ בְנֹתָ֗יו אַחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ן וְהִזְנוּ֙ אֶת־ בָּנֶ֔יךָ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: You shall make no molten gods for yourselves.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites.
God gave them commands.
God said, “Do not make molten gods for yourselves.”
Do not create idols from metal.
Do not worship these idols.
passages.original: אֱלֹהֵ֥י מַסֵּכָ֖ה לֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂה־ לָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: You are to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days at the appointed time in the month of Abib, you are to eat unleavened bread as I commanded you. For in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread.
This feast lasts seven days.
You must eat unleavened bread for these seven days.
You must do this at the appointed time in the month of Abib.
God gave this command.
In the month of Abib, God brought the Israelites out of Egypt.
passages.original: אֶת־ חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֨ת יָמִ֜ים תֹּאכַ֤ל מַצּוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ךָ לְמוֹעֵ֖ד חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָאָבִ֑יב כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב יָצָ֖אתָ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The first offspring of every womb belongs to Me, including all the firstborn males among your livestock, whether cattle or sheep.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God says, "The first offspring of every womb belongs to Me."
This includes every firstborn male among your livestock.
This includes cattle.
This includes sheep.
passages.original: כָּל־ פֶּ֥טֶר רֶ֖חֶם לִ֑י וְכָֽל־ מִקְנְךָ֙ תִּזָּכָ֔ר פֶּ֖טֶר שׁ֥וֹר וָשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: You must redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb; but if you do not redeem it, you are to break its neck. You must redeem all the firstborn of your sons. No one shall appear before Me empty-handed.
passages.sermon:
God gave these commands to Israel.
God said, “Redeem every firstborn donkey with a lamb.”
If you do not redeem the donkey, break its neck.
Redeem every firstborn son.
No one may appear before Me with empty hands.
passages.original: וּפֶ֤טֶר חֲמוֹר֙ תִּפְדֶּ֣ה בְשֶׂ֔ה וְאִם־ לֹ֥א תִפְדֶּ֖ה וַעֲרַפְתּ֑וֹ כֹּ֣ל בְּכ֤וֹר בָּנֶ֙יךָ֙ תִּפְדֶּ֔ה וְלֹֽא־ יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃

passages.text: Six days you shall labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest; even in the seasons of plowing and harvesting, you must rest.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people to work for six days.
God commands His people to rest on the seventh day.
God requires rest even during plowing season.
God requires rest even during harvest season.
passages.original: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲבֹ֔ד וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת בֶּחָרִ֥ישׁ וּבַקָּצִ֖יר תִּשְׁבֹּֽת׃

passages.text: And you are to celebrate the Feast of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
passages.sermon:
God commanded Israel to keep special feasts.
You must celebrate the Feast of Weeks.
You must bring the firstfruits of your wheat harvest at this feast.
You must also celebrate the Feast of Ingathering.
You must keep the Feast of Ingathering at the end of the year.
passages.original: וְחַ֤ג שָׁבֻעֹת֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לְךָ֔ בִּכּוּרֵ֖י קְצִ֣יר חִטִּ֑ים וְחַג֙ הָֽאָסִ֔יף תְּקוּפַ֖ת הַשָּׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God gave a command to the people of Israel.
God is the Lord.
God is the God of Israel.
All the males of Israel must obey this command.
Three times every year, all the males must appear before God.
They must come before the Lord God of Israel.
passages.original: שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה יֵרָאֶה֙ כָּל־ זְכ֣וּרְךָ֔ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֛י הָֽאָדֹ֥ן׀ יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For I will drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Israel.
God promised to drive out the nations before Israel.
God said He would make Israel’s borders larger.
God said no one would desire Israel’s land.
This would happen when Israel’s men went up three times each year.
They would go to appear before the LORD their God.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ אוֹרִ֤ישׁ גּוֹיִם֙ מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ וְהִרְחַבְתִּ֖י אֶת־ גְּבוּלֶ֑ךָ וְלֹא־ יַחְמֹ֥ד אִישׁ֙ אֶֽת־ אַרְצְךָ֔ בַּעֲלֹֽתְךָ֗ לֵרָאוֹת֙ אֶת־ פְּנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: Do not offer the blood of a sacrifice to Me along with anything leavened, and do not let any of the sacrifice from the Passover Feast remain until morning.
passages.sermon: God gave Israel laws for worship.\r\nGod said, “Do not offer the blood of My sacrifice with anything leavened.\r\nDo not let any part of the Passover sacrifice remain until morning.”
passages.original: לֹֽא־ תִשְׁחַ֥ט עַל־ חָמֵ֖ץ דַּם־ זִבְחִ֑י וְלֹא־ יָלִ֣ין לַבֹּ֔קֶר זֶ֖בַח חַ֥ג הַפָּֽסַח׃

passages.text: Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God gave them commands through Moses.
God said, “Bring the best of the firstfruits from your land.
Take these firstfruits to the house of the LORD your God.
Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.”
passages.original: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹא־ תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: The LORD also said to Moses, “Write down these words, for in accordance with these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD told Moses to write down these words.
These words are important.
The LORD made a covenant with Moses and with Israel based on these words.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כְּתָב־ לְךָ֖ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה כִּ֞י עַל־ פִּ֣י׀ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה כָּרַ֧תִּי אִתְּךָ֛ בְּרִ֖ית וְאֶת־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: So Moses was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights without eating bread or drinking water. He wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant—the Ten Commandments.
passages.sermon:
Moses stayed with the LORD.
He remained there for forty days.
He remained there for forty nights.
Moses did not eat bread during that time.
Moses did not drink water during that time.
Moses wrote on the tablets.
He wrote the words of the covenant.
He wrote the Ten Commandments.
passages.original: וַֽיְהִי־ שָׁ֣ם עִם־ יְהוָ֗ה אַרְבָּעִ֥ים יוֹם֙ וְאַרְבָּעִ֣ים לַ֔יְלָה לֶ֚חֶם לֹ֣א אָכַ֔ל וּמַ֖יִם לֹ֣א שָׁתָ֑ה וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב עַל־ הַלֻּחֹ֗ת אֵ֚ת דִּבְרֵ֣י הַבְּרִ֔ית עֲשֶׂ֖רֶת הַדְּבָרִֽים׃

passages.text: And when Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands, he was unaware that his face had become radiant from speaking with the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Moses was a prophet and leader of Israel.
Moses came down from Mount Sinai.
He carried the two tablets of the Testimony in his hands.
He had just come down from the mountain.
Moses did not know something had happened to him.
His face had become radiant.
This happened because Moses spoke with the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בְּרֶ֤דֶת מֹשֶׁה֙ מֵהַ֣ר סִינַ֔י וּשְׁנֵ֨י לֻחֹ֤ת הָֽעֵדֻת֙ בְּיַד־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה בְּרִדְתּ֖וֹ מִן־ הָהָ֑ר וּמֹשֶׁ֣ה לֹֽא־ יָדַ֗ע כִּ֥י קָרַ֛ן ע֥וֹר פָּנָ֖יו בְּדַבְּר֥וֹ אִתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Aaron and all the Israelites looked at Moses, and behold, his face was radiant. And they were afraid to approach him.
passages.sermon:
Aaron saw Moses.
All the Israelites saw Moses.
Moses had just come down from Mount Sinai.
Moses carried the two tablets of the covenant.
Moses’ face was shining.
His face was radiant because he had spoken with the LORD.
Aaron and all the Israelites saw that Moses’ face was radiant.
They were afraid.
They did not want to come near Moses.
passages.original: וַיַּ֨רְא אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְכָל־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה קָרַ֖ן ע֣וֹר פָּנָ֑יו וַיִּֽירְא֖וּ מִגֶּ֥שֶׁת אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: But Moses called out to them; so Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses called out to Aaron and the leaders.
Aaron was the brother of Moses.
Aaron and all the leaders of the congregation heard Moses.
Aaron and the leaders returned to Moses.
Moses spoke to Aaron and the leaders.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֲלֵהֶם֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֧בוּ אֵלָ֛יו אַהֲרֹ֥ן וְכָל־ הַנְּשִׂאִ֖ים בָּעֵדָ֑ה וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֲלֵהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And after this all the Israelites came near, and Moses commanded them to do everything that the LORD had told him on Mount Sinai.
passages.sermon:
All the Israelites are the people of Israel.
Moses is their leader.
The LORD is God.
God spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
After these things happened, all the Israelites came near to Moses.
Moses commanded the Israelites.
He told them everything that God had said to him on Mount Sinai.
Moses told them to do all that God had commanded.
passages.original: וְאַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֥ן נִגְּשׁ֖וּ כָּל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיְצַוֵּ֕ם אֵת֩ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה אִתּ֖וֹ בְּהַ֥ר סִינָֽי׃

passages.text: When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses spoke to the people.
Moses finished speaking with them.
Moses put a veil over his face.
passages.original: וַיְכַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה מִדַּבֵּ֖ר אִתָּ֑ם וַיִּתֵּ֥ן עַל־ פָּנָ֖יו מַסְוֶֽה׃

passages.text: But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he would remove the veil until he came out. And when he came out, he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded, and the Israelites would see that the face of Moses was radiant. So Moses would put the veil back over his face until he went in to speak with the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
The LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
Moses wore a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with Him, he removed the veil.
Moses kept the veil off until he came out from speaking with the LORD.
When Moses came out, he spoke to the Israelites.
Moses told the Israelites everything the LORD had commanded him.
The Israelites saw the face of Moses.
The skin of Moses’ face was radiant.
Afterward, Moses put the veil back over his face.
Moses kept the veil on until he went in again to speak with the LORD.
passages.original: וּבְבֹ֨א מֹשֶׁ֜ה לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ לְדַבֵּ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ יָסִ֥יר אֶת־ הַמַּסְוֶ֖ה עַד־ צֵאת֑וֹ וְיָצָ֗א וְדִבֶּר֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְצֻוֶּֽה׃ וְרָא֤וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת־ פְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֔ה כִּ֣י קָרַ֔ן ע֖וֹר פְּנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֑ה וְהֵשִׁ֨יב מֹשֶׁ֤ה אֶת־ הַמַּסְוֶה֙ עַל־ פָּנָ֔יו עַד־ בֹּא֖וֹ לְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּֽוֹ׃ס
